items.title: Pakistani Television Icon Bushra Ansari Set for Meadowvale Theatre Debut in September
items.summary: According to INsauga, veteran Pakistani entertainer Bushra Ansari is bringing her one-woman show to Meadowvale Theatre in Mississauga on September 5, marking the Canadian debut of the performance. INsauga reports Shaam-e-Tabassum, which translates to evening of smile, blends comedy, storytelling, satire and music, and will be performed mostly in Urdu with some Punjabi. Ansari told the outlet the humour she plans to bring draws directly from her own culture and language. INsauga notes the 70-year-old performer began her career at age nine and became a fixture of the golden era of Pakistani television, working first as a singer before moving into acting and comedy. Her career has earned her numerous honours, including the Presidential Pride of Performance Award in 1989, and INsauga reports she now lives in Richmond Hill while continuing to travel to Pakistan for work and appearing in Canadian television, including a role as Mommy Ji in Our Big Punjabi Family. According to the outlet, this follows Ansari's first one-woman show in 2023, Malika-e-Tabassum, which sold out all 20 of its performances and packed houses across Pakistan while exploring relationships, culture, feminism and the absurdities of everyday life.

items.title: City Opens 2027 Grant Applications for Mississauga Arts, Culture and Community Groups
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, not-for-profit organizations seeking funding for the 2027 calendar year can now begin applying to the city's Culture and Community Grant Programs. The city says funding is available to organizations of all sizes, including small and grassroots groups that expand recreational opportunities, local events and arts programming across Mississauga. According to the city, applicants are encouraged to review the grant guidelines and attend one of several virtual information webinars scheduled for September before applying. The city reports one stream supports emerging and established not-for-profit arts, culture and heritage organizations, aiming to improve residents' participation in and understanding of the arts. Another program, according to the city, provides annual and multi-year grants to community groups, including sports organizations and groups serving youth, older adults and inclusive recreation, that keep Mississauga residents active and engaged. The city notes a separate stream funds arts, heritage and cultural festivals and celebrations for residents and visitors, reflecting the value the city places on its cultural traditions.

items.title: Heavy Rainfall Strands Two Teens in the Credit River Before Peel Police Marine Unit Rescue
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, emergency crews rescued two teenagers who became stranded in the Credit River in Mississauga on Saturday after intense rainfall caused water levels to rise quickly. A Peel Regional Police spokesperson told CityNews that the rising water left the two individuals stranded on a small area of land within the river, without a boat or personal flotation devices. The outlet reports the teens contacted police themselves after realizing they were unable to safely make their way back to shore on their own. CityNews reports members of the Peel Regional Police Marine Unit responded to the scene along with several uniformed officers, paramedics and the fire department. Police told the outlet the two males were safely assisted out of the area and declined medical attention.

items.title: Peel Police Service Board Opens September Consultation on Youth Engagement Strategy
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the Peel Police Service Board's governance and human rights committee is hosting a community consultation session on September 15 at Peel Region headquarters to gather public feedback on the police's Youth Engagement Strategy, first launched in March 2025. Mississauga.com reports the session will open with a presentation from police outlining their preliminary youth engagement plan, after which members of the public will each get up to five minutes to make their own presentations to the committee. Police spokesperson Matt Carty told the outlet the service has a long-standing commitment to youth engagement and already runs a range of youth-focused education, prevention and mentorship initiatives, including the Youth in Policing Initiative, G1/G2 Driving, Boys 2 Men, Young Women's Mentorship and partnerships through ProAction Cops and Kids. In an email to Metroland Media cited by Mississauga.com, Carty said the current consultation process is meant to help inform the ongoing evolution of the strategy and support development of a more coordinated youth services model that strengthens how the service engages and supports young people. Mississauga.com notes the strategy has been evolving since its 2025 launch, with police framing the fall consultation as a key step toward shaping that more coordinated approach going forward.

items.title: Peel Police Data Shows Over 300 Vehicle Thefts Across Mississauga and Brampton in a Single Month
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police data shows more than 300 vehicles were reported stolen across Mississauga and Brampton over the past month. INsauga reports the count covers the 31-day period from July 22 to August 22, during which 304 vehicle thefts were recorded across the two cities. Of those, the outlet reports 175 thefts occurred in Mississauga and 126 in Brampton, with three additional incidents in Caledon falling under Peel police's jurisdiction. INsauga notes this report differs from some previous releases in that Peel Regional Police did not provide an updated breakdown showing how many of the cases had been solved, remained under investigation or were considered unsolved. The absence of that breakdown, according to the outlet, leaves residents without a clear picture of how much progress investigators have made on any of the reported thefts.

items.title: Culham Trail Upgrade and New Port Credit Pedestrian Bridge Get $8.7 Million Federal Boost
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, the federal government's Active Transportation Fund is providing $8.7 million to support two major local projects, upgrades to the Culham Trail and construction of a new pedestrian and cycling bridge in Port Credit. The city says the Culham Trail, which stretches through Erindale Park and Riverwood and draws more than 500,000 visitors a year, will see nearly four kilometres of the multi-use recreational trail modernized, along with enhanced flood protection and added amenities such as new seating, an outlook viewing area, a bike share system, upgraded signage and landscaping. According to the city, a new 65-metre bridge designed exclusively for pedestrians and cyclists will span the Credit River between Port Credit Memorial Park and the Port Credit Royal Canadian Legion, north of Lakeshore Road, linking Port Credit and the GO Station with the Mineola West neighbourhood. The city says the bridge was identified as a priority through the Lakeshore Corridor Transportation Improvements study and advances the broader Lakeshore Connecting Communities Master Plan for walking, cycling and access to destinations along the waterfront. Together, the city reports, the two projects are meant to improve connections across Mississauga and make active transportation options easier for residents to choose.
